_comment: Every step the Tapstitch web editor needs, as configuration rather than code. Tapstitch has no public API, so product creation goes through their editor; when they redesign it, this file is what gets repaired, not the runner. EVERY null below is unknown and must be filled in during the first live session with the editor open. scripts/tapstitch_publish.py refuses to run while any required value is null and prints exactly which ones are missing.
_first_session_checklist: ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. The save is PUT /api/designs/customized/templates/<templateId> and it carries piece, src, left, top, width, height, scaleX, scaleY and angle. Every step of product creation is a JSON call. See docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-editor-api.md. The selectors block below is probably dead, but NO CALL HAS BEEN REPLAYED yet, so it is kept until a scripted call is proven to work against one throwaway product.

PARTLY ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026. Tapstitch identifies colours by NUMERIC CODE (colorCode 8079,8088,8084,8085,8081 for the tee), so the API route cannot suffer a swatch-name typo. The check is NOT retired: shopify_fixups.py still matches on names, so colorway_renames_by_type must agree with whatever Tapstitch publishes to Shopify.

ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. Both files registered at 4386x5516, exactly the tee's real print area, and front and back got identical left/top/width/height/scale with only src differing. Uniform scale, no distortion.
ANSWERED 15 Sep 2026, YES. No re-crop was observed; the print-area-shaped file was accepted as-is.
Do one temple end to end by hand before letting the runner touch the catalogue.

urls._note: Filled from the address bar 15 Sep 2026. new_product was retired the same night: the observed flow never used one, because a design is created by POSTing the blank's SKU to api.create_template.

timing._note: Uploads of 4500x5100 PNGs and the publish-to-Shopify round trip are both slow. The Printify pipeline learned that publishes can far exceed a 240s window and still complete, so the runner confirms against Shopify rather than trusting the editor's own success state.

post_publish._set_product_type_note: LOAD-BEARING. Tapstitch publishes with an EMPTY productType, and every fixup in scripts/shopify_fixups.py is keyed on it, so colour ordering and the featured photo silently do nothing without this. Measured 14 Sep 2026; see docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-store-findings.md.
post_publish._delete_old_listing_note: TURNED OFF 16 Sep 2026, asked and confirmed by Evan explicitly. Was: delete the old Printify listing at the moment its replacement publishes, so the replacement inherits the same web address. That never worked. Shopify builds a new product's address from its TITLE and ignores whatever address just came free, so deleting freed the address and then left it unused; the crew's address had to be set afterwards with productUpdate(handle:), and its predecessor was permanently destroyed for nothing. Replacements now take their own address, old listings stay DRAFT, and scripts/easify_options.py sync repoints the dropdown links by reading handles from the live catalogue. This also keeps Printify intact as the way back, which deleting was quietly eating one product at a time.
post_publish._set_variant_back_images_note: LOAD-BEARING and not optional. Shopify binds each variant to the FIRST image of its colour at import and Tapstitch sends fronts first, so every variant lands on a near-blank garment and the product page opens there, whatever the gallery order says. MEASURED on the hoodie 16 Sep: posting the mockups back-first fixes the gallery but NOT the binding. Run scripts/tapstitch_variant_images.py after every publish; it is idempotent.

api._comment: The editor's own endpoints, observed 15 Sep 2026 and NOT yet replayed. Relative to https://www.tapstitch.com. See docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-editor-api.md for payload shapes and for what is still unverified.
api._method_note: save_design is a PUT. create_template, register_* and create_store_product are POSTs. The image bytes go by PUT straight to the OSS URL that retrieve_upload_data returns.

crew.name: Fleeced Sweatshirt
crew._colour_note: 5720 Black, 6551 Flower Gray. Read off the catalogue search on 16 Sep 2026 and CONFIRMED against the store-product prefill, which is what Tapstitch will send Shopify: it names them 'Black' and 'Flower Gray', matching garments/crew.json. The swatch-name risk is closed for this blank. A THIRD colourway, 6672 Oat Gray, is also US-fulfilled and is left out because the config lists two; it is light, so it would need the black art.

hoodie.name: Oversize Fleeced Hoodie
hoodie._colour_note: 6674 Navy Blue, 5720 Black, 6645 Gray, 6657 Coffee, 6650 Dark Purple (shown as Mauve), 6654 Klein Blue (shown as Royal Blue). Evan's lineup off real mockups, 16 Sep 2026, and CONFIRMED against the store-product prefill, which named all six exactly as garments/hoodie.json does. It replaced a lineup that was stale and partly impossible: the config had listed 'Dark Gray' and 'Dark Green', neither of which exists on R00286. Navy Blue leads because it is the storefront_first_color. EDEN GREEN 6655 ADDED 22 Sep 2026, Evan's call. US-fulfilled (LA). Its catalogue chip is RGB(5,57,45), which is the DYE SAMPLE and far darker than the photographed garment; true_colors_all.json carries RGB(46,97,75), measured off a real Tapstitch mockup the way every other entry was. Generating from the chip would have produced a near-black hoodie.

api._status: PROVEN END TO END for all three garments. create_template, the signed OSS upload, save_design, create_store_product and distribute have all run against the live account; a crew and a hoodie were published to the live Shopify storefront on 16 Sep 2026. distribute takes a LIST of STORE-PRODUCT ids (a third id kind), so a batch is one call.
_traps: x-oss-meta-author is a SIGNED header on the OSS upload. Omit it and the PUT is a bare 403 with a valid, fresh signature. Its value is retrieve-upload-data's `author` field.
Upload lands on the OSS bucket host; a design must reference it on files.tapstitch.com. Same path, different host.
A rejected call still returns HTTP 200. Check the envelope's `code`, not the status line.

A malformed save returns code 10001 'System error, please refresh and try again', which says nothing. It means a required key is missing: virtualConfig, mockupConfig, or per-object clipId / customAreaId / designPart / flipX / flipY / visible.
srcDetails.srcId is NOT required, so the multipart user_cover_img/save call can be skipped entirely.
api._placement: DERIVED 16 Sep 2026, no longer copied. get_template()'s craftItemDto.customArea states each side's print-area rectangle on the 700x700 canvas; tapstitch_api.print_areas() reads it and placement() turns it into the editor's geometry. Checked against the 15 Sep tee, which it reproduces to within the half pixel the editor rounded away. The rectangles differ per garment AND per side: tee 260x327 both sides, crew 210x281 back and 209x275 front.

size_guide._note: EVAN'S RULE, 16 Sep 2026: the size guide goes in the description and it is imperial. Not metric, not both. This is a real trap rather than a preference, because Tapstitch's store-product prefill comes back with IMPERIAL and METRIC BOTH selected, so the default behaviour ships inch/cm column pairs. The runner takes sizeGuide.descriptionHtml['IMPERIAL'] from the prefill and appends it to description.content; there is no sizeGuide key in the POST body, the table is baked into the description at create time.
size_guide._bare_numbers_caveat: Tapstitch's IMPERIAL table carries NO unit label anywhere: 'Chest 23.62' with nothing saying inches. reference/garment-copy/*/size-guide.html says 'Measurements (inches)' and is written to Shopify afterwards, which is what the live tee ended up with on 15 Sep.

_selectors_note: The click-path selectors that used to sit here were DELETED 16 Sep 2026. They described driving the Tapstitch web editor by clicking, which stopped being the plan on 15 Sep when the editor turned out to be a plain JSON API (docs/discovery/2026-09-tapstitch-editor-api.md). They were kept as a retired block and that was a mistake: on 16 Sep they were read as live and led to the conclusion that browser automation was still needed before a catalogue run, which was false and had already been false for a day. Product creation is tapstitch_api.py, driven by scripts/tapstitch_run.py. The only thing a browser is still used for is reading the logged-in cookies out of the dedicated Chrome profile (tapstitch_api.session).
